source.title: Weil positivity and Trace formula, the archimedean place

quotes: THEOREM 1 -- the source's main positivity statement, with EVERY hypothesis
Let g in Cc^infty(R+*) have support in [2^-1/2, 2^1/2] and Fourier transform vanishing at i/2 and 0. Then W_infty(g * g^*) >= Tr(theta(g) S theta(g)^*).
DEFINITION (section 3; the corpus calls it Definition 3.1)
Let G be a locally compact abelian group and f in L^1(G, dg). We say f is positive definite when its Fourier transform is pointwise positive, i.e. f^(t) >= 0, for all t in G^.
PROPOSITION 2 -- BOAS-KAC. ### THE STATEMENT OF THE SHAPE THE ORDER ASKS FOR

Let f in Cc^infty(R) have support in the interval [-A, A] (A > 0). The following conditions are equivalent: 1. The Fourier transform f^ is pointwise positive. 2. There exists g in Cc^infty(R) with support in [-A/2, A/2] such that f = g * g^*.
THE RH CRITERION, AND THE CLASS IT QUANTIFIES OVER
RH <=> sum_v W_v(g * gbar^#) <= 0, for all g in Cc^infty(R+*) with g~(z) = 0 for all z in F.
WHY THE SUPPORT IS RESTRICTED, IN THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS
In this paper we consider the simplest instance of this strategy, namely when the support of the test function is contained in the interval (1/2, 2) subset R+*.
THE VANISHING CONDITIONS AS AN IDEAL
The vanishing conditions int f(rho) rho^(+-1/2) d*rho = 0 define an ideal J in the convolution algebra Cc^infty(R+*).
